CaNrg1 is the Candida albicans transcriptional regulator being characterized in the study, functioning within this organism to control morphogenesis and virulence-associated gene expression.
CaNrg1 contains a conserved zinc finger domain, indicating a DNA-binding structural feature that supports promoter recognition and transcriptional repression.
CaNrg1 interacts specifically with the NRE in vitro, consistent with direct binding to promoter elements that mediate repression.
CaNrg1 represses hypha-specific genes; loss of CaNrg1 derepresses these genes, showing direct negative regulation of the hyphal gene-expression program.
CaNrg1 suppresses the hypha-specific gene expression program, thereby limiting hyphal differentiation and associated pathogenic behavior.
CaNrg1 represses yeast-hypha morphogenesis, acting as a negative regulator of the developmental transition that underlies filamentation.
Inactivation of CaNrg1 causes filamentous and invasive growth in Candida albicans, demonstrating that CaNrg1 normally restrains this pathogenic growth phenotype.
Loss of CaNrg1 increases sensitivity to some stresses, indicating that CaNrg1 contributes to stress-response robustness.
Inactivation of CaNrg1 attenuates virulence, linking this transcriptional repressor to pathogenic fitness in Candida albicans.
CaNrg1 represses a subset of CaTup1-regulated genes, indicating overlap and coordination between CaNrg1 and CaTup1 regulatory programs.
The paper concludes that CaNrg1 appears to target CaTup1 to a distinct set of virulence-related functions, implying functional coupling between the two repressors.
CaNrg1 represses virulence factors among its target genes, thereby modulating pathogenic potential.
CaNrg1-mediated repression of the ALS8 promoter depends on NREs; deletion of two NREs from this promoter releases it from repression.
ScNrg1 represses transcription in a Tup1-dependent fashion, indicating a functional relationship with Tup1 in transcriptional repression.
Tup1 is the corepressor whose regulated gene set overlaps with the genes repressed by CaNrg1, including hypha-specific genes and virulence factors.
NREs within the ALS8 promoter are required for Nrg1-mediated repression; deletion of two NREs abolishes this regulatory effect.
The NRE is the promoter element specifically bound by CaNrg1 to mediate transcriptional repression.
Expression of hypha-specific genes supports the yeast-to-hypha developmental program; their derepression is associated with filamentous growth and morphogenesis.
Virulence factors contribute mechanistically to pathogenicity, so their repression or derepression directly affects the virulence phenotype.
By repressing virulence-related genes and morphogenetic programs, CaNrg1 functionally targets the virulence phenotype in Candida albicans.
